purpose: Entrectinib is a targeted cancer medicine used to treat certain types of solid tumors in adults and children that have a specific gene change called an NTRK fusion. It is also used to treat a type of lung cancer called ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer. Your doctor will test your tumor to make sure this medicine is right for you.
how_it_works: Your cancer cells have an abnormal protein switch that tells them to keep growing out of control. Entrectinib works by blocking that faulty switch, which helps slow down or stop the cancer from growing and spreading. Think of it like putting a lock on the "go" signal that the cancer cells rely on.
common_side_effects: Tiredness or weakness, swelling in your hands or feet, dizziness, constipation or diarrhea, nausea or vomiting, changes in your sense of taste, weight gain, shortness of breath, numbness or tingling in hands or feet, and muscle or joint pain.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious heart problems including a slow or irregular heartbeat. It may also cause bone fractures more easily, liver problems, vision changes, and serious nervous system effects like confusion or memory problems. It can harm an unborn baby, so effective birth control is very important during treatment and for some time after. Tell your doctor right away if you feel faint, have chest pain, notice vision changes, or feel unusually confused.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 600 mg taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. Swallow the capsules whole — do not crush or chew them. Your doctor may lower your dose if you have side effects. Always take it exactly as your doctor instructs and try to take it at the same time each day.
